subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should portable Agent Bundles be a core-owned import/export feature, a plugin/ClawHub bundle API, or a narrower plugin-SDK extension for agent registration?
rationale: The current repo has only manual agent CRUD and adjacent plugin/skill bundle pieces; choosing the permanent owner boundary and security model affects config, workspace, auth, skills, channel routing, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Design a core bundle contract
options.body: Core owns a versioned manifest, dry-run validation, safe import/export transaction, and explicit non-secret allowlists before implementation starts.

options.title: Add a plugin API first
options.body: Core exposes only the missing generic agent registration/import primitives, and publishable ClawHub packages own concrete bundle distribution.

options.title: Defer as external workflow
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not add core or SDK surface until maintainers see a smaller proven bundle package that identifies the exact missing API.

recommendation.title: Design a core bundle contract
recommendation.body: Core owns a versioned manifest, dry-run validation, safe import/export transaction, and explicit non-secret allowlists before implementation starts.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent history on agent CLI/config flow and is best placed among the observed owners to choose the product/API boundary.
